title: Chestnut Oak: Ancient Chestnut Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: An eastern oak named for its chestnut-like bark. In Washington DC, a national co-champion 737 cm round is the largest known tree in the city.
intro: The chestnut oak is an eastern North American oak, named for bark that looks like the American chestnut's, and unusual among oaks in resprouting readily from a cut stump. In 2023 Casey Trees named the chestnut oak in Washington's Battery Kemble Park the city's largest known tree, 737 centimetres round, and American Forests lists it as a national co-champion. Its trunk is low and many-stemmed, on a hill the Union Army fortified in 1861, and every account puts it there before the Civil War. At Gettysburg, chestnut oaks fill the fenced Copse of Trees that Pickett's Charge aimed at in 1863, though the Park Service says none of today's trees stood then. Elsewhere the species has travelled. Boulder says the largest in Colorado grows in Chautauqua Park, and Wisconsin's champion is a planted arboretum tree near Poynette. St. Louis's Tower Grove Park calls its own the king of the hill.
